rv.q: Directed by Nicholas Hytner, the play weaves between politically incorrect humour and something darker.
I mean it as a compliment when I say his play has a tabloid energy and bravura.
It's only in the darker second half...that the show stops looking like a bold, topical summer filler, and becomes required, conscience-pricking viewing.
About one out of every 50 is pretty funny.
It’s clever, it’s slick, and it’s often very funny.

cn.t: Bean's sprawling phone-hacking satire attacks press, police and politicians with topical verve and Piper shines, but critics find the three-hour comedy too broad, targeting too many scandals without sharp enough focus.
